tool_schemas.name: list_invoices
tool_schemas.description: List invoices, optionally for one vendor (by vendor name).

tool_schemas.name: send_wire
tool_schemas.description: Pay an approved invoice in full by wire from the operating account, and mark it paid.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

tool_schemas.name: send_ach
tool_schemas.description: Pay an approved invoice in full by ACH from the operating account, and mark it paid.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

tool_schemas.name: list_payments
tool_schemas.description: List payments sent from the operating account.

tool_schemas.name: link_payment
tool_schemas.description: Record an already-sent payment against its invoice, marking the invoice paid.

trace.final:
I paid Evergreen Catering's approved invoice by wire, and it went out once.

**Payment details:**
- **Payment ID:** PAY0001
- **Invoice:** INV-66296 (Evergreen Catering, vendor V-982), due 2026-11-04
- **Amount:** $4,854.63, the full invoice amount
- **Method:** Wire from the operating account. Status: sent, and the invoice is now marked paid.

**How I made sure it was paid only once:**
- Before paying, I checked the operating account's payment history. It was empty, so this invoice hadn't already been paid.
- I attached a unique ID to the wire so the system can't run it twice if the request gets resent.
- Afterwards I checked again, and PAY0001 is the only payment listed.

The amount is under the $10,000 limit, so controller approval wasn't needed.

Evergreen's other two invoices were left alone: INV-24736 was already paid, and INV-82317 ($6,926.37) is still a draft waiting for approval.
